{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABd69Vqw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhHcC1M", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 260, "title": "Remove redundant Graph Library sidebar and simplify navigation around graphs and launch settings", "body": "## Problem

The latest Graph Library layout (#255, implemented in PR #257) looks cleaner at first glance, but its **navigation model and action hierarchy are still inconsistent**:

1. Sidebar **Graphs** and **Launch Settings** look like distinct page/view choices; both sections are already simultaneously visible in the two-column workspace. Clicking either only focuses/scrolls to that section (`[data-section]` handler in `extension/graph-library-page.js`), leaving the screen effectively unchanged.
2. Sidebar **Graph Editor** links to the *currently selected* graph (`#editor-link` is dynamically rewritten), while the graph's details already have a clear **Edit graph** action. The sidebar mixes top-level navigation with context-dependent commands.
3. Sidebar **Live** is not a normal page destination: it focuses an existing Live window or instructs the user to open Live via the extension toolbar. It behaves differently from other nav items.
4. The top-of-sidebar **Local processing** label does not establish a useful brand or navigation hierarchy and takes visual space.
5. The UI makes users reason about four interaction zones—sidebar, graph cards, graph detail dialog, Launch Settings—where two task areas would be sufficient.

**Owner-approved direction (2026-11-10): remove the Graph Library sidebar entirely.** Keep the clean two-column layout but make the page self-explanatory through grouping, not redundant navigation.

This supersedes the **sidebar/navigation** portion of #255, while retaining its useful card presentation and the separation introduced in #253.

## Proposed information architecture

A single **Graph Library** page, no left navigation rail:

```text
Graph Library                                                    [Models]
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┌──────────────────────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ Graphs                [+ New]    │  │ Launch Settings                 │
│ [ Search graphs…          ] [⋯]  │  │                                 │
│                                  │  │ Live Window                     │
│ ┌──────────────────────────────┐ │  │ [ Meeting Notes             ▾ ] │
│ │ Voice Input             [⋯] │ │  │                                 │
│ │ Speech to text               │ │  │ Web Page Microphone       [ON] │
│ ├──────────────────────────────┤ │  │ [ Voice Input              ▾ ] │
│ │ Meeting Notes           [⋯] │ │  │                                 │
│ │ Transcription / summary      │ │  └─────────────────────────────────┘
│ ├──────────────────────────────┤ │
│ │ Translation             [⋯] │ │
│ └──────────────────────────────┘ │
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

Illustrative graph names only; render the user's actual saved graphs. Favor spacious alignment, simple typography, minimal decorative framing, no permanent wall of help text.

### A. Remove the misleading sidebar

- Remove `<aside class="library-sidebar">`, its `Local processing` brand/heading and the entire **Graphs / Launch Settings / Models / Live / Graph Editor** sidebar menu from **the Graph Library page**.
- Remove `[data-section]` click/focus/scroll handlers, `aria-current="location"` behavior and unused sidebar styling. There must not be "navigation" that only focuses a panel that is already visible.
- Keep **Graph Library** as the single clear page heading.
- Retain a compact, discoverable **Models** link/action as a utility in the page header (use actual existing route). Do not replace the removed sidebar with another row of redundant pseudo-tabs.
- **Do not add a fake Live navigation item**. Live remains launched by its actual toolbar workflow; if contextual help is needed, show it briefly and truthfully near relevant settings, not as a misleading page link.
- **Do not add a top-level Graph Editor item** on the Library page. Editing a graph is a contextual action tied to a specific graph; put it on the graph card/action menu and/or inside the graph detail view.
- Existing Graph Editor/Models/Live pages must remain functional and able to return to the Library as appropriate; avoid unrelated redesign of those screens.

### B. Main workspace: only two coherent task areas

**Left: Graphs / graph management**

- List saved graphs as clean cards/rows with name, optional short description and discoverable secondary **⋯** actions. Keep **+ New Graph**, search, sort/filter, JSON import, empty/recovery states.
- Selecting/opening a graph leads to a focused detail dialog/subview with graph preview, **Edit graph**, rename/description/save, Duplicate, Export, Delete, model file status and recovery as before. An existing directly available **Edit graph** command is also fine if it clearly targets the clicked graph.
- Ensure no ambiguity about whether clicking a card merely selects it or **opens details**: use visual affordances, labels/accessibility, and consistent behavior. No unexplained "selected" state that changes a hidden target for global navigation.
- Maintain unsaved changes protection, draft recovery, revision conflicts, export/delete safeguards and focus return after dialogs.

**Right: Launch Settings / launch bindings**

- Always visible beside the Graphs area on suitable desktop widths, not a separate navigation destination.
- **Live Window** graph dropdown and **Web Page Microphone** dropdown with separate ON/OFF switch. Labels name the *launch surface*, not graph purposes.
- Selecting a graph in the left panel **must not change** either launch assignment. Changing either dropdown must not change the active graph detail. Selecting a Web graph must not automatically enable website controls or request host permission. Turning OFF retains its assignment.
- Keep compatibility validation, permission consent only after explicit enablement, denial/error states, next-session snapshot semantics, storage sync, and independent session execution.
- Avoid redundant "using..." strings already present in selectors. Display errors/actionable help only when applicable; concise disclosure for website permissions.

### C. Responsive, accessibility and code hygiene

- Desktop: simple page header above a two-column layout (proportions can adapt to graph list/controls). Remove the **200px sidebar tax** and use freed width for content.
- Narrow viewports: stack Graphs then Launch Settings with visible headings; no dead navigation, sideways overflow or clipped dialogs. Don't make the second section inaccessible when a graph detail dialog is open.
- Support keyboard and touch access, labeled buttons/menus/selects, meaningful focus restoration, accessible permission/error messages, and forced-colors / contrast behavior.
- Prefer scoped changes in `extension/graph-library.html`, `extension/graph-library.css`, `extension/graph-library-page.js` and the affected UI tests. Remove orphaned `#editor-link` references after deleting the sidebar; do not break graph-editor linking from graph details. Avoid creating a new generic navigation architecture.
- Preserve graph data schema, assignments, model handling, Live/runtime behavior, Web microphone permissions and the work in #256/#258 (independent Live/Web execution). No unrelated modifications to X/Twitter rich editor support.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Graph Library desktop page shows **one heading + two side-by-side primary panels: Graphs and Launch Settings**, without a global left sidebar or redundant in-page pseudo-navigation.
- [ ] Neither **Local processing**, nor separate top-level **Graphs / Launch Settings** selection controls, nor top-level **Graph Editor** are shown on this screen.
- [ ] Models remains reachable with one unobtrusive, working utility link; Live is not falsely represented as a regular page destination.
- [ ] Opening and editing a graph is obvious; graph cards and menus target the clicked graph, not an unrelated previously selected item; all existing graph-management controls still work.
- [ ] Launch dropdowns, Web microphone ON/OFF, explicit consent/permissions and graph eligibility retain their existing behavior independently of library browsing.
- [ ] Editing/canceling/saving graph details, keyboard focus return, mobile layout, filtering, import/export, conflicts and storage recovery continue to work.
- [ ] Browser/UI tests assert no redundant sidebar or pseudo-nav, visible desktop two-panel layout, and correct graph-specific edit actions. Update old #255 assertions/screenshots/docs and record tests actually executed.

## Context

- #253: separates managing generic graphs from configuration of launch entry points.
- #255 / PR #257: introduced the current sidebar + paired-panel design. **This issue deliberately removes the sidebar** after actual use showed misleading/redundant controls.
- Do not revive the old `Use this graph for` controls or make Launch Settings a second copy of the Library.
